answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the delta check immediately, the tundra audit keeps the resolved set and the ocean replay exposes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 107 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 107 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
